Object Text: The AEB feature shall be implemented as a distributed AUTOSAR application composed of seven application SWCs allocated to the AEB partition on ECU_AEB_Main: SWC_AEB_SensorFusion, SWC_AEB_RiskAssessor, SWC_AEB_Controller, SWC_AEB_BrakeActuator, SWC_AEB_SafetyMonitor, SWC_AEB_VehicleState, and SWC_AEB_HMI. The feature shall detect an imminent forward collision, warn the driver, and automatically request service braking to avoid or mitigate the collision.
Notes: Top-level AEB feature architecture; req_type=FUNCTIONAL; UNECE R152

Object Text: The AEB function shall be active over the vehicle speed range 10 km/h to 60 km/h inclusive for car-to-car scenarios, per UNECE R152. The function shall deactivate the automatic braking demand below 10 km/h and above 60 km/h while continuing to monitor and report AEB availability status.
When a collision is deemed imminent, the AEB Controller shall request a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s2 to the service braking system, per UNECE R152 emergency braking requirement.
Notes: R152 minimum emergency braking demand; req_type=SAFETY

Object Text: The AEB feature shall provide a forward collision warning using at least two of the acoustic, haptic, and optical modalities. The warning shall be issued no later than the start of the emergency braking intervention.
A driver-initiated brake or accelerator action that exceeds the AEB braking demand shall override and cancel the AEB braking request. The override shall be detected within one control cycle.

The AEB feature shall publish its availability and state (OFF, STANDBY, ACTIVE, WARNING, BRAKING, FAULT) to the gateway via provided port PP_AEBStatus with Sender-Receiver interface IF_SR_AEBStatus, updated every 10 ms.

On ECU startup, the AEB SWCs shall complete RAM and ROM self-tests, initialize all internal states to safe defaults (no braking demand, no warning), and remain in STANDBY until vehicle state and sensor signals are validated.
Notes: Safe-state init before any runnable runs; req_type=FUNCTIONAL

Object Text: Every AEB requirement shall be traceable to one software runnable, one MUD flowchart step, and one or more unit test cases. All safety-relevant signals shall be protected with AUTOSAR E2E Profile 2.
SWC_AEB_SensorFusion shall execute RE_FuseObjects cyclically every 10 ms to time-align and fuse the radar object list and the camera object list into a single fused object list.

SWC_AEB_SensorFusion shall read RP_RadarObjects (SR IF_SR_ObjectList, up to 64 objects) and RP_CameraObjects (SR IF_SR_ObjectList, up to 32 objects) via required ports. Each object shall carry object ID, longitudinal distance, lateral offset, relative speed, object class, and existence probability.

SWC_AEB_SensorFusion shall publish the fused object list via PP_FusedObjects (SR IF_SR_ObjectList, up to 128 objects) every 10 ms. Each fused object shall carry a confidence score in [0.0, 1.0] and a source mask indicating radar, camera, or both.

RE_FuseObjects shall time-align radar and camera objects to the current cycle using each sensor's last valid measurement timestamp and the object relative speed. Objects older than 200 ms shall be dropped.

RE_TrackAssociate shall associate a radar object and a camera object to the same fused track when their longitudinal distance and lateral offset each agree within 0.5 m AND their relative speed agrees within 2.0 m/s. Exactly one radar object may associate to one camera object.

When one sensor source (radar or camera) is unavailable, RE_FuseObjects shall continue using the remaining sensor, set the source mask accordingly, and mark the fused confidence reduced. The fusion shall set bit[1] of the PP_FusedObjects status when running single-source.

RE_FuseObjects shall reject fused objects whose longitudinal distance is negative (behind ego), whose relative speed magnitude exceeds 80 m/s, or whose existence probability is below 0.4. Rejected objects shall not appear in PP_FusedObjects.

RE_FuseObjects shall set a per-source timeout flag when a sensor provides no valid objects for more than 100 ms. The flags shall be exposed on the PP_FusedObjects status for consumption by SWC_AEB_SafetyMonitor.
SWC_AEB_SensorFusion shall expose the fusion thresholds (association distance 0.5 m, association speed 2.0 m/s, drop age 200 ms, minimum probability 0.4) as calibration parameters stored in ROM.
RE_FuseObjects shall not allocate dynamic memory and shall complete within 2.0 ms worst case on its 10 ms cycle, keeping the computation path fixed.
Notes: No dynamic memory; 2.0 ms WCET; req_type=CONSTRAINT

Object Text: SWC_AEB_RiskAssessor shall execute RE_AssessCollisionRisk cyclically every 20 ms to compute Time-To-Collision (TTC) and collision probability for the most critical fused object in the ego lane.

RE_AssessCollisionRisk shall compute TTC = distance / relative_speed for each fused object with positive relative speed (approaching), where distance is longitudinal range in meters and relative_speed is in m/s. Objects with relative_speed <= 0 shall be assigned TTC = TTC_MAX (no collision).

RE_AssessCollisionRisk shall select the critical object as the fused object with the smallest valid TTC whose lateral offset places it within the ego path, using a path half-width of 1.0 m plus the object half-width.

RE_AssessCollisionRisk shall raise the FCW warning request when the critical object TTC falls to 2.6 s or below. The warning request shall be latched until TTC rises above 2.9 s (hysteresis) to prevent warning flicker.
Notes: FCW TTC=2.6 s, release 2.9 s; req_type=SAFETY

Object Text: RE_AssessCollisionRisk shall request partial braking (40 percent) when the critical object TTC falls to 1.6 s or below. The partial braking request shall remain until TTC rises above 1.8 s.

RE_AssessCollisionRisk shall request full braking (100 percent) when the critical object TTC falls to 0.6 s or below. The full braking request shall remain until the collision is resolved or the driver overrides.

RE_AssessCollisionRisk shall compute collision probability as a continuous value in [0,1] from the critical TTC using a piecewise-linear map: 0.0 at TTC >= 3.0 s, 0.5 at TTC = 1.6 s, and 1.0 at TTC <= 0.6 s, clipped to [0,1].

SWC_AEB_RiskAssessor shall publish PP_RiskAssessment (SR IF_SR_Risk) every 20 ms containing critical_TTC (0.01 s resolution), collision_probability (0.001 resolution), risk_level enum {NONE, WARNING, PARTIAL, FULL}, and critical_object_id.

RE_AssessCollisionRisk shall suppress the braking escalation (partial or full) while vehicle speed is below 10 km/h, but shall continue issuing the FCW warning when a pedestrian-class object is detected crossing ahead.
SWC_AEB_Controller shall execute RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand cyclically every 10 ms to convert the risk assessment into a deceleration demand and a braking mode.

RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall select the highest braking level among the driver demand, the AEB risk level, and any fail-safe request. AEB shall win over driver braking during active emergency braking unless the driver override condition holds.

RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall map the risk level to a deceleration demand: NONE to 0.0 m/s2, WARNING to 0.0 m/s2 (warning only), PARTIAL to 4.0 m/s2, and FULL to 9.0 m/s2. The FULL demand shall satisfy the R152 minimum of 5.0 m/s2.

RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall limit the rate of change of the commanded deceleration to 15 m/s3 using a first-order rate limiter to avoid wheel lock and occupant discomfort. The limiter state shall be preserved between cycles.

RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall cancel the AEB braking demand when the driver brake pressure exceeds the AEB-equivalent brake pressure by 10 bar, or when the accelerator pedal is pressed beyond 80 percent of full travel. The override shall clear the AEB demand within one 10 ms cycle.
RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall issue a brake pre-fill command (pre-tension pads, target 5 bar) when the risk level is WARNING, so the service brake is prepared before full braking onset.

SWC_AEB_Controller shall publish PP_BrakeDemand (SR IF_SR_BrakeDemand) every 10 ms containing deceleration demand in m/s2 (resolution 0.01), brake mode enum {NONE, PREFILL, PARTIAL, FULL, FAILSAFE}, and a demand counter for E2E.
Notes: Brake demand output + E2E counter; req_type=INTERFACE

Object Text: When SWC_AEB_SafetyMonitor reports a plausibility fault, RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall enter FAILSAFE mode and command a controlled braking demand of 6.0 m/s2 unless vehicle speed is below 10 km/h.
RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall increment a 16-bit demand counter on every published PP_BrakeDemand. The counter shall roll over from 0xFFFF to 0x0000 and shall be used by the E2E protect routine.

RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall ignore a risk assessment whose critical object is outside the ego path (lateral offset magnitude above 1.5 m) when vehicle speed is above 40 km/h, to reduce false braking on curves.

RE_ArbitrateBrakeDemand shall accept RP_ABSStatus (boolean) from the brake system and reduce the deceleration demand to the ABS-allowed maximum when ABS reports active wheel slip, preventing conflict between AEB and ABS.

SWC_AEB_Controller shall expose the TTC-to-demand thresholds, deceleration rate limit 15 m/s3, override thresholds (10 bar, 80 percent), and pre-fill target 5 bar as calibration parameters stored in ROM.
SWC_AEB_BrakeActuator shall execute RE_CommandBrake cyclically every 5 ms to convert the deceleration demand into a brake pressure command and apply it via the brake booster.

RE_CommandBrake shall convert the deceleration demand to a target brake pressure using P_target = decel_demand * K_veh_mass / K_brake_gain, where K_veh_mass is the calibrated vehicle mass (kg) and K_brake_gain is the calibrated deceleration-per-bar gain (m/s2 per bar).
RE_CommandBrake shall ramp the commanded brake pressure toward P_target at a maximum rate of 200 bar/s on application and 300 bar/s on release to avoid pressure spikes.

RE_CommandBrake shall read back the achieved brake pressure via RP_BrakePressureFeedback and compare it to the commanded value. A deviation exceeding 15 bar for more than 50 ms shall be reported to SWC_AEB_SafetyMonitor as a brake actuation fault.
SWC_AEB_BrakeActuator shall publish PP_BrakePressure (SR IF_SR_Pressure) every 5 ms containing the commanded brake pressure (bar, resolution 0.1) and a status flag indicating actuation health.
On initialization and whenever no braking demand is active, RE_CommandBrake shall command 0 bar (no braking) and set the actuation status to IDLE.
RE_CommandBrake shall clamp the commanded brake pressure to the range [0, P_MAX], where P_MAX = 250 bar. Commands below 1 bar shall be treated as 0 bar to avoid residual pressure.
SWC_AEB_BrakeActuator shall expose K_veh_mass, K_brake_gain, ramp rates (200 bar/s apply, 300 bar/s release), deviation threshold 15 bar, and P_MAX 250 bar as calibration parameters stored in ROM.
SWC_AEB_SafetyMonitor shall execute RE_MonitorSafety cyclically every 5 ms to perform plausibility checks, E2E verification, watchdog triggering, and degraded-mode management.

RE_MonitorSafety shall compare the fused critical object's longitudinal distance and relative speed against the raw radar measurement each 5 ms. A deviation above 1.0 m or 3.0 m/s for more than 3 consecutive cycles shall raise a sensor plausibility fault.

RE_MonitorSafety shall verify the E2E Profile 2 protection on all safety-relevant input signals (RP_RadarObjects, RP_CameraObjects, RP_VehicleSpeed, RP_YawRate). A counter mismatch or CRC failure shall trigger the corresponding fault after 2 consecutive failures.
RE_MonitorSafety shall trigger the hardware watchdog via Rte_Call every 5 ms. A missed trigger shall cause the ASIL-D hardware watchdog to reset the ECU.

RE_MonitorSafety shall transition the AEB feature to DEGRADED mode (braking limited to 4.0 m/s2, warning disabled) when a single sensor source fails, and to FAILSAFE mode (controlled braking 6.0 m/s2) when both sources fail or an actuation fault is present.

RE_MonitorSafety shall report every detected fault to DEM via Dem_ReportErrorStatus and store the fault snapshot (fault code, TTC, vehicle speed, timestamp) in NVM via NvM_WriteBlock(NvM_AEB_FaultLog).
SWC_AEB_SafetyMonitor shall publish PP_SafetyStatus (SR IF_SR_Safety) every 5 ms containing the AEB mode enum, an active fault bitmask, and E2E verification status per source.
RE_MonitorSafety shall perform RAM checksum and ROM CRC-32 self-tests at startup. Any failure shall set the AEB feature to FAULT mode and inhibit automatic braking until ECU service.
SWC_AEB_SafetyMonitor shall expose plausibility thresholds (1.0 m, 3.0 m/s, 3 cycles), E2E failure count 2, and the degrade and derate levels as calibration parameters stored in ROM.
SWC_AEB_VehicleState shall execute RE_UpdateEgoMotion cyclically every 10 ms to update ego vehicle speed, longitudinal acceleration, yaw rate, and steering angle from vehicle sensors.

SWC_AEB_VehicleState shall read RP_VehicleSpeed (SR IF_SR_Speed, range 0-350 km/h, resolution 0.01 km/h, 10 ms cycle) and RP_WheelSpeedFL, RP_WheelSpeedFR, RP_WheelSpeedRL, RP_WheelSpeedRR (four wheel speeds) via required ports.

RE_UpdateEgoMotion shall validate RP_VehicleSpeed against the four wheel speeds. If the difference exceeds 3 km/h for more than 100 ms, the vehicle speed signal shall be flagged invalid and the last valid value held.
SWC_AEB_VehicleState shall read RP_YawRate (range -100 to +100 deg/s, resolution 0.01 deg/s) and RP_SteeringAngle (range -720 to +720 deg, resolution 0.1 deg) for ego-path estimation.
SWC_AEB_VehicleState shall publish PP_VehicleState (SR IF_SR_EgoState) every 10 ms containing vehicle speed, longitudinal acceleration, yaw rate, steering angle, and a signal-validity bitmask.
RE_UpdateEgoMotion shall set the standstill flag when vehicle speed is below 0.5 km/h for more than 200 ms, and clear it when speed exceeds 1.0 km/h (hysteresis).
SWC_AEB_HMI shall drive the forward collision warning to the instrument cluster via PP_HMIWarning (SR IF_SR_HMI) containing the warning level enum {NONE, VISUAL, VISUAL_ACOUSTIC, VISUAL_HAPTIC}.

RE_UpdateWarning shall activate at least two warning modalities (visual plus acoustic, or visual plus haptic) whenever the FCW warning request is active, satisfying the UNECE R152 collision warning requirement.
RE_UpdateWarning shall update the cluster warning state on a DataReceivedEvent of PP_RiskAssessment, and shall clear the warning within 500 ms of the risk level returning to NONE.
SWC_AEB_HMI shall relay the AEB availability and fault status to the cluster for the tell-tale lamp, updated every 100 ms, using PP_AEBStatus.
